s.t: From Fivetran’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. With Fivetran, customer data arrives in their warehouses, canonical and ready to query, with no engineering or maintenance required. We’re proud that more organizations continue to leverage our technology every day to become truly data-driven.

Fivetran is building data pipelines to power the modern data stack for thousands of companies.
We’re seeking a Principal Software Engineer to contribute to the technical architecture, design and development of Fivetran’s Managed Data Lake product offering. As part of a senior engineering team, you’ll partner with product and engineering teams to build scalable, high-performance systems, advance open-source technologies, and set technical standards that raise the bar across the organization.
This is a full-time remote position based out of Germany.
Technologies You’ll Use
Java, C++, Postgres, Temporal, gRPC
AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, Grafana
Iceberg, Polaris, Delta Lake, Parquet, DuckDB

Partner closely with product teams to understand requirements and design cutting-edge new capabilities that go directly into customer’s hands.
Design, develop, implement, and operate highly reliable large-scale data lake systems in cooperation with a dedicated data lake engineering team.
Contribute to open-source projects such as DuckDB and Polaris.
Embrace Fivetran innovations with open-source standards and toolsets.
Analyze fault-tolerance and high availability issues, performance and scale challenges, and solve them.
Ensure operational excellence of the services and meet the commitments to our customers regarding security, reliability, availability, and performance.
Set technical directions and influence cross-functional teams.

6+ years of hands-on or research experience with high-performance relational data management systems.
Deep understanding of infrastructure & software optimizations and performance engineering to drive significant performance, latency, and availability improvements.
Proven track record of leading and delivering large and complicated projects.
Strong development skills in Java and C++.
Solid experience with public clouds (AWS, Azure, GCP).
Demonstrated knowledge of columnar storage formats.
Growth mindset and excitement about breaking the status quo by seeking innovative solutions.
Excellent team player who is consistent in making everyone around you better.
Bonus Skills
Strongly prefer an MS or PhD in Computer Science, ideally focusing on database management and/or storage engines.

About Variant Security
Variant Security is securing the world's critical fleets for the AI era. Today nearly every device runs identical software, so a single exploit can cascade across an entire fleet of satellites, drones, vehicles, and defense systems, and AI has made finding that one exploit cheaper than ever.

Variant breaks that pattern, so compromising one device gives an attacker nothing against the rest and no single failure can bring down the fleet. AI made exploits cheap, and we make them useless, already protecting systems across aerospace, defense, and active conflict zones.

As a Compiler Engineer, you'll build and own the compiler technology at the core of Variant's product, turning cutting-edge diversification into something that ships. You'll work across two areas, the compiler itself and the systems and tooling that run it at fleet scale, with real ownership rather than narrow ticket work.

You'll have a direct line to the founding team, immediate impact on what customers run, and room to grow from a strong early-career engineer into the owner of a core domain. Variant Security is securing the world's critical fleets for the AI era.

Develop and extend compiler passes that harden builds against exploitation
Reverse engineer and analyze the generated binaries to validate transformations
Measure security and performance impact across x86, AArch64, and RISC-V targets
Build tooling in modern C++ and Python, and integrate the compiler into CMake and customer CI/CD

Master's degree, or equivalent hands-on experience, in cybersecurity or computer science
Hands-on experience with binaries, whether reverse engineering, exploitation, or vulnerability research

Low-level systems background, spanning embedded, firmware, OS internals, or ELF/PE formats, linkers, and loaders

Work on rare, hard problems where compilers meet binary security, the kind most engineers never get to touch
Early-stage equity and competitive compensation on the ground floor
Learn directly from a founding team with deep security, compiler, and space-systems pedigree (top-tier security research, DARPA, SpaceX)
See your work protect real fleets across aerospace, defense, and active conflict zones
Based in the Bochum office, with regular collaboration across Germany and the U.S. and the chance to work from or visit the US team

Join Our Team We are the Audi Revolut F1® Team.
Audi Revolut F1 Team is the official factory team of Audi, as the brand enters the FIA Formula 1 World Championship for the first time in 2026.
The team is based in three locations: the power unit is developed by Audi Formula Racing GmbH at the Audi Competence Center Motorsport in Neuburg, Germany; the chassis is engineered and race operations are managed from the state-of-the-art facilities of Audi Motorsport AG in Hinwil, Switzerland; while the Audi Motorsport Technology Centre UK in Bicester, United Kingdom, provides a foothold in the heart of 'Motorsport Valley', with direct access to top F1 talent and key strategic partners.
What you need? The mindset of an athlete. If you are someone for whom giving up isn’t an option and limits are just something to be overcome, you can bring Vorsprung durch Technik to Formula 1 with us. Become part of this unique project and make motorsport history.

Design, develop, test and deliver high-quality full-stack software solutions, including backend services, frontend applications, APIs, databases and integrations.

Support enterprise scaling of AI adoption by contributing to practical use cases, secure integration patterns, cost-aware im plementation and approved-tool usage.
Contribute to architecture, software engineering standards, CI/CD, testing, deployment automation and maintainable cloud-native engineering practices.
Remain flexible in acquiring domain knowledge, primarily around aero processes but also across wider digital transformation initiatives in the organization.

Strong full-stack software engineering capability, including backend and frontend development using modern languages and frameworks such as C#, Python, TypeScript, ASP.NET Core, FastAPI , React, Vue, Svelte or equivalent technologies.
Hands-on experience with GenAI technologies, including practical use of LLMs, AI coding assistants, prompt engineering and integration of AI capabilities into applications.

About CoLab At CoLab, we help mechanical engineering teams bring life-changing products to market years sooner. CoLab is the AI platform for driving stronger engineering decisions.

Every design review in CoLab builds a knowledge repository of design feedback, decisions, and lessons learned - which AI agents draw from to flag issues on future designs before they compound. The more your team works in CoLab, the smarter it gets and the faster you arrive at the ideal design.

Companies like Ford, Komatsu, and Johnson Controls use CoLab to catch issues earlier, eliminate rework cycles, and bring products to market faster. Founded in St. John's, Newfoundland, CoLab has grown quickly from our first customer in 2019 to a rapidly scaling company.

We've recently been recognized on Deloitte's Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, and named a Canadian company to watch by The Globe and Mail and Financial Post. About the Role Modern engineering teams invest a significant amount of time and money on simulation.

Before anything gets built, teams need confidence that a design is going to work: structurally, thermally, aerodynamically, etc. Simulation is one of the main ways they build that confidence. But the way teams share and review simulation results to make decisions is still pretty broken.

Engineers are exporting videos, taking screenshots, dropping them into PowerPoint, and then trying to make decisions through email threads, meetings, or disconnected slide decks.

The actual decision-making ends up separated from the underlying simulation data, which means context gets lost, feedback is hard to trace, and important engineering knowledge disappears into the workflow. CoLab already helps engineering teams review CAD, capture feedback, and make better design decisions in one connected workspace.

Now we’re extending that same idea into simulation. The goal is simple: make simulation results collaborative, reviewable, and traceable in the same way CoLab does for CAD today. We’re starting a new product team focused on bringing simulation review into CoLab.

As one of the first engineers on that team, you’ll help define how simulation data gets ingested, visualized, discussed, and connected back to real engineering decisions.

There are a lot of interesting technical problems here: large datasets, high-performance visualization, viewer interactions, data pipelines, and user experiences that need to work for mechanical engineers doing critical product development work.

The first phase is about learning the product, the customers, and the review workflows we already support today. You’ll spend time embedded with our Engineering Reviews team, learning how engineers collaborate in CoLab, where the current product is strong, and where simulation creates a new set of problems we need to solve.

From there, you’ll help build the foundation for a new Simulation team - not just technically, but from a product perspective as well. We want to build something customers actually need and will use in their day-to-day work, and that requires a highly product oriented approach.

Our Ideal Candidate You're the kind of developer who wants to understand why a feature matters before deciding how to build it. You enjoy owning complex technical problems, but you also enjoy talking with product managers, designers, and customers to understand what success actually looks like.

You make thoughtful technical decisions independently and know when to bring others into the conversation. Experience working with simulation software is a significant advantage. Maybe you've worked with FEA, CFD, multiphysics simulations, scientific visualization, or engineering data platforms.

You understand the kinds of problems engineers are trying to solve. This is a good fit for someone who likes ambiguity, wants to work closely with our product and leadership teams, and cares about the connection between technical decisions and customer value.

You’ll have a meaningful role in shaping both the architecture and the user experience for a new capability that we think can become a major part of engineering review in CoLab. What You'll Do
Help design and build CoLab's next-generation simulation review capabilities.
Build services that ingest and process simulation data from industry-standard engineering software.
Develop high-performance visualization experiences capable of displaying large simulation datasets.
Partner closely with Product, Design, and customers to validate ideas before building them.
Spend time embedded with the Engineering Reviews team to develop deep product and customer understanding before transitioning onto the Simulation team.
Contribute to architectural decisions that will shape this product area for years to come.
Improve performance, scalability, and reliability as simulation capabilities grow.
Collaborate with engineers across the platform to ensure simulation becomes a seamless part of the broader CoLab experience.

Full-ownership software engineer responsible for building a new system in TypeScript that will replace our existing PHP system, while maintaining the current PHP system throughout the transition. This is not a hand-off role — you take a problem from requirement to production and own it there. You'll work across both stacks, make technical decisions, and be accountable for what you ship.
We expect you to use AI coding tools as a core part of how you work. Not occasionally — daily. Your velocity, code quality, and problem-solving should reflect effective AI tool use. What we care about is judgment: understanding what you ship, making the right decisions, and knowing when to push back on AI output.
This description applies across experience levels (L1–L4). Interview depth and expectations are calibrated to your level.
Tasks

Features from requirements to production: you break them down, build them, ship them, monitor them
Technical decisions within your scope, with clear trade-off reasoning
Quality of your code and the areas you touch
Responding to incidents and dev-escalations in your domain
Building the new TypeScript system that will replace the legacy PHP platform
Maintaining and supporting the existing PHP system throughout the transition

1. Feature Development
Take feature requests, break them into tasks, estimate, and deliver independently
Build the new TypeScript-based system designed to replace our existing PHP platform
Maintain and support the current PHP system in parallel, until the new system is fully migrated
Write clean, tested, production-ready code that meets team standards
Make technical decisions for features and explain trade-offs clearly
Monitor your features in production — logs, metrics, alerts
Leave the codebase better than you found it (refactor, document, reduce debt)
2. Production Ownership & Incident Response
Respond to dev-escalations with urgency — investigate issues, communicate findings, contribute to resolution
Participate in incident response: at all levels, you are expected to show up, help investigate, and support resolution
L4+: Drive incident response for your domain — coordinate investigation, delegate tasks, communicate status to stakeholders, and ensure post-mortems happen
Write runbooks and keep documentation current as you build
Share on-call rotation after ramp-up period
3. Code Quality & Testing
Write unit and integration tests as part of feature work, not as an afterthought
Participate actively in code reviews — give thoughtful feedback, act on feedback you receive
Identify edge cases and risks during planning, not after deployment
4. AI-Augmented Development (Expected, Not Optional)
Use AI coding tools daily: code generation, debugging, test writing, exploring unfamiliar parts of the codebase, code review acceleration
Your output should be measurably faster because of AI tools
You understand everything you ship — AI is an accelerator, not a replacement for judgment
L3+: Help teammates develop effective AI workflows; contribute to team standards for AI tool use
L4+: Set team standards for AI tool usage — evaluate what delivers real value, ensure quality isn't sacrificed for speed
5. Collaboration
Work closely with Product, Design, QA, and other engineers
Contribute meaningfully to sprint planning and technical discussions
L3+: Mentor L1/L2 engineers through code reviews, pairing, and sharing knowledge

s.h: What You Bring To This Role
s.t:
Technical Environment
Primary stack: TypeScript/Node.js for the new system you'll build, and PHP 7.4/8+ with Laravel for the existing system you'll maintain during the transition.
Infrastructure: MariaDB, Redis, AWS (EC2, RDS, CloudWatch, SQS, S3), Docker, GitHub Actions CI/CD
This role requires active, hands-on TypeScript experience and past professional experience with PHP. Hands-on experience integrating payment platforms such as Stripe and PayPal is required .

L1: Works on well-scoped tickets with guidance. Learning the codebase and practices. Uses AI tools to learn faster and ship more.
L2: Independently owns features. Minimal guidance needed on implementation. Noticeably faster because of AI tool usage.
L3: Leads small projects. Mentors L1/L2. Improves the codebase proactively. Teaches effective AI workflows.
L4: Technical authority for a domain. Drives cross-team projects. Sets team AI standards. Drives incident response.

Early on, you'll ship your first feature to production, understand the core architecture, and get your local development environment set up. From there, you'll be independently shipping features end-to-end and contributing to code reviews. As you grow further, you'll contribute meaningfully to technical discussions and handle dev-escalations in your area.
Shared rotation (~1 week/month after ramp-up). Critical: 15 min. High: 1 hour.

The TFH and World tech stacks make this possible: the Orb verifies real, unique people, World ID proves it privately, and World App puts these capabilities, and more, in people’s hands. Together, they add a human layer to an AI-driven internet.
World is already running at a global scale. More than 17 million people across 160 countries have verified with World ID, and more new Orb verifications take place each week. Developers are integrating World ID to build safer online experiences and create spaces where real people can participate, earn, and be recognized in ways AI simply can’t replicate.

At Code, we design and build digital products and platforms for a range of clients.
We’re looking for a Lead Software Engineer who wants to stay hands-on. You’ll write production code, make and shape technical decisions, and support a small group of engineers.
This isn’t a role where you step away from engineering to manage from the side lines. You’ll be involved in the day-to-day work: thinking through architecture, reviewing code, tackling difficult problems and helping the team find sensible ways forward when things get complicated.
You’ll line manage 3–4 engineers, with regular 1:1s and responsibility for supporting their development. A big part of the role is helping other engineers get better at what they do — not by having all the answers, but by giving them the support and technical direction they need.
You’ll work closely with delivery managers, designers, product managers, principal engineers and clients. Sometimes that means working through a difficult technical problem; sometimes it means challenging a requirement, explaining a trade-off or finding a simpler way to achieve the same thing.
Most of our web work is built around TypeScript, React and Next.js, alongside APIs, cloud services, headless platforms and other backend technologies.

Write production code across the stack and stay involved in the day-to-day engineering work.
Take the lead on technical decisions within the team, bringing in principal engineers and others when decisions have wider implications.
Help turn large or difficult problems into work the team can understand and deliver.
Line manage 3–4 engineers through regular 1:1s, feedback, coaching and career conversations.
Review code, talk through designs and help engineers make good technical decisions rather than simply making those decisions for them.
Work with delivery, design, product and client teams to understand what we’re trying to achieve and find an appropriate technical approach.
Keep an eye on the things that make software good to work with and reliable in production: testing, CI/CD, observability, security, accessibility and performance.
Help design and evolve web platforms that integrate with APIs, headless systems and third-party services.
Contribute to the wider engineering team at Code, sharing what works, challenging what doesn’t and helping us improve how we build software.

You’ve probably already worked as a senior or lead engineer in a team building and shipping software.
You’re comfortable taking responsibility for technical decisions, but you also know when a decision needs wider discussion.
You’ll need strong hands-on TypeScript experience and good experience with modern web development using React, Next.js or similar frameworks.
You should also be comfortable working beyond the frontend. That might mean Node.js, C#/.NET or another server-side technology. We care more about your ability to understand APIs, backend services and how the whole system fits together than whether your experience exactly matches our stack.
We’d also expect you to be comfortable with many of the things that come with building modern web platforms: APIs, server-side rendering, automated testing, CI/CD, cloud services, web performance and integrating with third-party or headless systems.
You’ll need to be able to explain technical ideas clearly. Some conversations will be with engineers; others will be with designers, delivery people, clients or stakeholders who don’t particularly care how the codeworks. Being able to adjust how you communicate matters.
Experience line managing engineers is useful, but it isn’t essential if you’ve already spent time mentoring, coaching and supporting other developers and want to take on that responsibility formally.
We don’t expect you to know everything. Experience with Azure, AWS or GCP is useful, as is experience across both TypeScript and C#/.NET, but neither is a requirement. We’re more interested in good engineering judgement, curiosity and someone who can help a team make sensible decisions and ship good software.

Design, implement, validate, and maintain robust in-house embedded software for key FIA Formula 1 platforms, notably the FIA Standard ECU and Accident Data Recorder, to monitor and enforce regulatory compliance.
Lead end-to-end multi-system integration across control units, sensors, vehicle communication buses, telemetry networks, and FIA data-analysis suites.
Translate complex sporting, technical, and operational requirements into high-integrity software architectures, detailed specifications, and rigorous verification plans.
Develop specialized simulation, test, and data-analysis tools to accelerate software validation, support regulatory evolution, and guarantee operational readiness.
Execute functional and integration testing on bench and vehicle environments in close collaboration with F1 teams, power unit manufacturers, and electronics suppliers.

Build and scale in-house engineering capabilities, reinforcing the FIA’s operational independence and responsiveness to emerging technical demands.

Development strategy and regulatory support

Define specifications for future FIA electronic architectures, safeguard FIA intellectual property, and contribute technical input to F1 working groups.
Race and test support

Analyse real-time vehicle telemetry to verify regulatory compliance and resolve cross-system software anomalies in collaboration with teams and manufacturers.
